unit_keying.batch_key_inputs: writer, target_table, tf, range_start, range_end, sha256(sorted chunk symbols), code_key, apr_hash, input_digest, unit_key
unit_keying.chunk_composition: split_symbol_chunks(sorted(universe passed), 25): depends on the symbol list given to --symbols
unit_keying.stability_conclusion: A completed 1d unit is invalidated only by a change to its own 25-name chunk, the code sha, the APR snapshot, the horizon or its own bars. Adding timeframes never touches it (tf is in the key). Adding the 229 holds does NOT touch it IF the later stage passes --symbols <holds only> (or any set disjoint from these 1,273) with --tf 1d: new chunks, new keys. Running the 1d stage over the merged 1,502 list would re-chunk (sorted interleave) and recompute everything.
unit_keying.choice_made: --symbols is the explicit non-hold list; chunk size left at the APR 25. Later 1d stage: --symbols <229 holds> --tf 1d --data-horizon 2026-10-01 from this tree. Intraday stage: any symbol set, tfs differ.
unit_keying.horizon: pinned --data-horizon 2026-10-01 (exclusive); it is in range_end for 1d, so every stage and every resume must pass the same value. Bars from 2026-10-01 on are not in these features.
unit_keying.compression_caveat: run_rebuild_stage compresses only for a full-scope run (no --symbols, no --tf), which would re-plan with different chunks and recompute 1d. Stage 1 therefore leaves feature_vectors_v2 uncompressed; compression needs a standalone _batch_utils.compress_completed_chunks call after all stages, or a rule change. Not decided here.
